To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

i) the CNN architecture has a strong impact on performance; ii) dataset scale has a strong impact and larger datasets lead to higher performance; iii) the spatial image context has a strong impact, and larger spatial context leads to higher performance; and iv) pre training on natural images can be beneficial.

1) the CNN architectures with more layers perform better than the shallower models, 2) the performance of CNN based CADe system is highly dependent on the size and quality of the training set, 3) transfer learning can be useful when there is not enough training data, but the pre training model is too large for the available computational resources.

1) the VGG16 architecture is the best choice among all CNN models we have evaluated for both LN detection and ILD classification; 2) a larger training set size and the use of a spatial context model can both improve performance; 3) pre training on ImageNet is not always useful, and it can even degrade performance.
